title: claimspec v1 — concerns
description: A concern is one sentence a human writes that generates faults across a whole surface: it says WHERE to look and WHICH shapes of break are relevant. It is the rung between writing nothing and writing a claim per behaviour. A concern is never a claim and never becomes one by itself — it says where to look, the probe says what it found, and a human states the sentence worth defending. Nothing in this document is a promise about the code; only a claim is that.

id.description: Declaring an id that matches a built-in REPLACES it, which is how a project retunes a default for an ORM or a layout this tool does not recognise. The replacement is reported, never silent.

statement.description: The sentence, in plain language. It describes a KIND of promise, not one behaviour: "every write persists the data it was given", not "the register action stores password_hash". The second is a claim.

targets.description: Where this concern applies. `write-sites` asks the write enumerator. `glob` matches paths. `changed` defers to whatever diff the caller is already measuring — a concern does not re-derive what the gate computed.

faultClasses.description: Which producers are relevant. `null` or absent means every class, the honest default for a concern with no shape to narrow by. Narrowing is what makes one sentence useful across two hundred files: a persistence concern that also reported every altered return value would bury the payload findings it exists to surface.
